title: Why an ice cube melts faster in fresh water than in salt water
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: Does ice melt faster in salt water or fresh water?
Why does ice melt slowly in salty water?

figure.name: x-compare
figure.verdict: Sinking meltwater stirs; floating meltwater insulates

explain.say: Drop one ice cube into a glass of fresh water and another into very salty water, both at room temperature. Surprisingly, the cube in fresh water melts first.

explain.say: In fresh water, the icy meltwater is colder and denser than the warm water around it, so it sinks. Warmer water keeps flowing in to touch the cube and melt it.

draw.verdict: Sinking meltwater stirs; floating meltwater insulates

explain.say: In salt water, the meltwater is fresh, so it is less dense than the salty water and floats. A cold layer gathers around the cube and keeps warm water away, so it melts slowly.

faq.q: Does an ice cube melt faster in salt water or fresh water?
faq.a: In a still glass at room temperature, it melts faster in fresh water, because the cold meltwater sinks and keeps warm water moving past the ice.
asks: Which melts ice faster, salt water or tap water?

faq.q: Why does cold meltwater sink in fresh water?
faq.a: Water at 0 degrees is a little denser than water at room temperature, so in a glass of fresh water it sinks to the bottom and starts a stirring current.
Salt sprinkled straight onto ice does lower its melting point. Here the bigger effect is the floating layer of fresh, cold meltwater that wraps the cube and shields it from the warm salty water.
asks: Why doesn't the salt help it melt?

faq.q: How can I see this at home?
faq.a: Freeze ice cubes with a drop of food colouring in them. Put one in fresh water and one in very salty water, and watch where the coloured meltwater goes.
asks: How do I do the ice cube experiment?

faq.q: Where does this matter in nature?
faq.a: Melting ice at the poles adds fresh water that can float on top of the salty ocean in a layer, which changes how the ocean mixes.
asks: Does melting sea ice float on the sea?

facts: Sea water is denser than fresh water because of its dissolved salt, about 1.025 grams per cubic centimetre compared with about 1.000.
Fresh water is densest at about 4 degrees Celsius.

quiz.why: Fresh meltwater is less dense than salt water, so it floats around the cube and keeps the warmer salty water away.

wrong.0: Both glasses started at the same room temperature.
wrong.1: Salt does not harden ice; it is the floating cold layer that slows melting.
